subject: re-st
title: RE.ST.------TRS.
description: Diagram in WAC-14, paired with v1-p216-1. (C)RE-ST (restructuralism — Braxton's term he prefers over 'innovation') is crossed with TRS (transition). The diagram poses what restructuralism's relationship to transition actually requires structurally — situated against Braxton's WAC-6 claim that he 'uses the word [restructuralism] instead of innovation since innovation does not semantically give enough emphasis on the progressive route of a given information readaptation.' Three upstream feeds converge on RE-ST: PROG-CONT (progressional continuance), TRS (the crossing partner), and IST-S-ALGN (isolated systematic alignment); INDIV-TD (individual tendencies, fed in turn by AFI affinity insight) also feeds RE-ST. RE-ST outputs to ALT-ACT (alternative activism) → SPT-DY (spiritual dynamics). A separate chain runs INFO-AF-B (information affinity basis) → AFTF (affinity transfer) and → INTR (interpretation). Structural argument: restructuralism is over-determined upstream (progressional continuance, transition, isolated systematic alignment, and affinity-insight-grounded individual tendencies all feed it), and its productive output is alternative activism leading to spiritual dynamics — the very channel Braxton names as the missing hinge in post-Wagnerian western culture. The information-affinity-basis chain runs in parallel, producing affinity-transfer and interpretation as separate outputs, neither directly involved in restructuralism's transition relation.
